anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 4,173,100,000, investments 1,128,300,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 17,870,800,000 (tagged_plus_current; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 0 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 2,469,261,188 at 2026-10-27 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 38,181,700,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 38,181,700,000 (FY2026 revenue: company guidance midpoint 37,000,000,000 (36,900,000,000-37,100,000,000, issued 2026-10-28) + (track-record ratio 1.1136 - 1) x the Q4 FY2026 guided midpoint 10,400,000,000 = 38,181,700,000; First fiscal-year revenue guide: 36.9-37.1B (issued 2026-10-28 with Q3 results; 9M reported 26.61B, so the remainder is the Q4 guide 10.3-10.5B). Amphenol beat its quarterly revenue guide midpoint in every recorded quarter (ratio 1.06-1.19, mean 1.11; Q3 2026 1.094) and Q3 orders were 12.2B (book-to-bill 1.19), above the Q4 guide: the track-record ratio applied to the Q4 remainder is the honest reading. (evidence dc_guid_fy26_rev, dc_guid_q4_rev, web:pf_rel_20261028_1; source tier guidance)); growth 65.3% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 45,949,244,022/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 3.0 years in base (maturing stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 23.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 13.3% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 0.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 3.1% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 11.5% or above 27.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from organic growth 37.8%, not the current fiscal year's 65.3% that includes acquired revenue (pro forma revenue for the same months a year earlier 19,368,600,000 against 16,655,700,000 reported (16.3% bought): organic growth 37.8% against 59.8% reported); the acquired revenue is a level shift in the current year: 23.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 12.1% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.7% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 23.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 13.3% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 32.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 18.3% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 7.2% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 17.7% a year over 10 fiscal years (15.0% after 2.35% expected inflation); 3% of companies with sales of $12,000-25,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 2.7% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (27.4% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 27.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 21.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 5.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 24.9% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 27.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 26.0% over 5 years, then holds. below type-typical: base closes 60% of the gap from 27.7% to 30.0% (not below the best of 3 years 25.4%). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 27.4% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 27.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 29.0% over 5 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 5.0%, capped at the type ceiling 45.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 25.0% and margins above 29.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Evidenced source: engineering co-design and qualified supply in AI racks (exclusive DensiLink in GB200/GB300, PaladinHD2 named for VR NVL72) plus breadth; gross margin 39.3% vs TE about 35.6%. Not strong: TE holds about 30% of the GB300 backplane, FIT enters in 2027 and every rack generation is re-competed.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 30.0% is competed away (0.0% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 20.0% against a demonstrated ROIC 29.3% (Ku 8.1% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (demonstrated ROIC 21.8% vs hurdle 8.1% (excess 0.58); ROIC variation 18% over 5 years (stability 1.00); gross margin 36.9%, range 5.6% over 5 years (margin 0.00))). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 0.5% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 20% of its level over 5 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 4.0% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 3.9% = min(3-year average capex 3.9%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.4296812069083213, type range (0.3, 1.0), base 1.43, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.03). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 23.2% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 100%). The stub's revenue change excludes 3,600,000,000 of bought revenue (analyst input: CommScope Connectivity and Cable Solutions (CCS) (closed 2026-01-09) brought 3,600,000,000 of the current year's revenue step; Pre-deal size from the Q3 2026 10-Q pro forma note (CommScope included from 2025-01-01): pro forma 9M 2025 net sales 19,368.6M against reported 16,655.7M = 2,712.9M for nine months, about 3.6B a year. The 2026 contribution is guided at 5.1B; the step above the pre-deal size is CommScope's own growth and stays charged as growth. The 10.5B price is already in the opening debt.): the acquisition paid for it and its price is in the opening balance, so it is not charged again as growth reinvestment.

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.197 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 0.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.00 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 25.0%: 3-year effective 21.5% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(2 months of cash costs, today's cash), 4,152,720,070 in the first period rising to 4,173,100,000 (base) of today's cash 4,173,100,000: about 1.69 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 44.2% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 17,870,800,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 2.06% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 7.98% (risk-free + 3%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 1,128,300,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 8.59%: table rate 8.59% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:maturing +0.50%, country_risk +0.11%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.20%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.06% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 2.06% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 5.0%) = 8.59% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 16,722,120,070 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 337,049,108,860 gives debt weight 4.7% (converged, 3 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 7.98% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.09% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.09% (the table without stage:maturing +0.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 8.59%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 21.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 27.3% of NOPAT with ROIC 16.4% (adequate moat, Ku+1pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.1%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: base terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 26.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 24.9% of NOPAT with ROIC 20.0% (adequate moat, Ku + 50% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+2pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.1%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 29.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 20.3% of NOPAT with ROIC 24.5% (adequate moat, Ku + 71% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+4pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.1%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.0%.

assumptions.rationale: The FactBook carries no revenue consensus at as_of (not retrieved or not stored); nothing is fabricated. Growth is anchored on trailing growth instead.

assumptions.label: analyst override: growth_anchor
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of growth_anchor: FY2027 growth is almost all organic (CommScope closed 2026-01-09, inside FY2026). assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of mature_margin: GAAP operating margin (after SBC and acquisition amortization) 19.1-20.7% in FY2020-FY2024, 25.4% in FY2025, 27.7% TTM to September 2026, 29.5% in Q2 and Q3 2026 (Q3 tariff recovery only 15M, so the run rate is real). Base 26%: between FY2025 and TTM: the AI-mix step (about +5-6 points over the pre-AI 20.5%) stays, the peak operating leverage of a 65%-growth quarter is given back. Bull 29%: the Q3 run rate holds as AI mix stays high and CommScope's margin keeps improving (accretion guide raised three times). Bear 21%: back to the company's own 2020-2024 range as AI volumes fall. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2020, pf_revenue_fy2020, pf_operating_income_fy2022, pf_revenue_fy2022, pf_operating_income_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_operating_income_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2025, nm_operating_income_ttm_2026_09_30, nm_revenue_ttm_2026_09_30, pf_operating_income_q_2026_09_30, pf_revenue_q_2026_09_30, dc_fact_adj_opm_q3_2026, dc_fact_ieepa_q3_2026; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of tax_rate: GAAP Q3 2026 rate 27.4% includes 60M of discrete foreign tax items (about 2.1 points on about 2.8B pre-tax), a one-off; Q2 GAAP 25.3%. assumptions.label: analyst override: sales_to_capital
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of sales_to_capital: Amphenol's own 3-year incremental sales-to-capital (engine series, 2026-10-26 run) is 1.43, and it counts acquisition goodwill as capital, so it is conservative for organic growth. The organic record needs less: FY2025 revenue +51.7% (about +38% organic) with capex 4.3% of revenue; 9M 2026 capex 1.10B = 4.2% of sales with operating cash flow 4.76B; Q3 capex 4.47% of sales and FCF 1.62B. Same in all scenarios: the bear is a demand fall, not a change in the capital a dollar of sales needs. (evidence pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_capex_fy2024, pf_capex_fy2025, pf_cfo_fy2025, pf_capex_q_2026_09_30, pf_cfo_q_2026_09_30, dc_fact_capex_9m_2026, dc_fact_ocf_9m_2026, dc_kpi_capex_pct_q3_2026, web:pf_10q_20261030, web:pf_10k_20260211; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: analyst override: terminal_roic
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of terminal_roic: From the engine's ROIC series on Amphenol's companyfacts (2026-10-26 run; NOPAT over equity + debt - cash - investments, goodwill included), FY2006-FY2025: minimum 16.4% (FY2017), median 19.4%, average 20.4%, FY2025 29.3% (AI peak, not used). Base 20% = 20-year average; bear 16.4% = 20-year low (CommScope's 10.5B of capital earning about 6% so far pulls toward it); bull 24.5% = best pre-AI year. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2020, pf_operating_income_fy2022, pf_operating_income_fy2024, pf_operating_income_fy2025, web:pf_10k_20260211, pf_goodwill_fy2025; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-08-01: cash 466,869,000, investments 297,389,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 0 (none_tagged; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 0 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 187,951,918 at 2026-08-25 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-08-01 and as_of 2026-10-28: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2027-04-29 revenue differs from 2,525,601,350 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2027-04-29 revenue 2,525,601,350 (FY2027 revenue: company guidance midpoint 2,469,964,600 (2,469,964,600-2,469,964,600, issued 2026-09-01) + (track-record ratio 1.1050 - 1) x the Q2 FY2027 guided midpoint 530,000,000 = 2,525,601,350; FY2027 (ends 2027-04-29): the CFO's 'more than 85%' growth statement on the 2026-09-01 call (ex_tr_20260901, a third-party transcript copy saved verbatim; not restated in the written release ex_rel_20260901) = a FLOOR of 2,470.0M (rp_g_rev_fy27_floor, 1.85 x FY2026 1,335.1M), raised from 'more than 80%' in June. A floor is not a midpoint: Credo has beaten every one of 7 quarterly guides (ratio mean 1.105) and delivered its FY2026 annual statement ('more than 200%' vs +205.7%). The engine adds (1.105 - 1) x the Q2 guide midpoint 530M = about +55.7M, so about 2,525.6M (+89%). This adjustment stands for the 'more than' above the floor, not for an expected 10% Q2 beat: the last two beats were only +1.6% and +1.9%. Cross-check only: attributed consensus FY2027 2,503.1M (range 2,470.0-2,583.7M, 19 analysts). Arithmetic: Q1 479.0M + Q2 530M = 1,009M, so the year needs a second half of about 1,517M (about 640M in Q3 and 877M in Q4): it carries the optical inflection management described (>600M optical), which fx_q3rev, fx_optical and fx_fy27rev test. It replaces the engine's year-to-date extrapolation (about 2.87B in the 2026-10-26 run). (evidence rp_g_rev_fy27_floor, rp_g_rev_q2fy27, web:ex_rel_20260901, web:ex_tr_20260901; source tier guidance)); growth 89.2% vs the last report. The stub 2026-10-28..2027-04-29 runs at 2,758,376,558/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-08-01 to 2027-04-29.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 5.00% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-04-29 above 42.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: -5.0% in FY ending 2028-04-29, 2.1% in FY ending 2032-04-29, 4.5% in FY ending 2047-04-29; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-04-29 below 18.5% or above 53.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 89.2% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 132.2% for reference): 42.0% in FY ending 2028-04-29, 17.2% in FY ending 2032-04-29, 5.2% in FY ending 2047-04-29; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-04-29 below 42.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 65.0% in FY ending 2028-04-29, 30.6% in FY ending 2032-04-29, 6.0% in FY ending 2047-04-29; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 25.7% a year over 10 fiscal years (22.8% after 2.35% expected inflation); 2% of companies with sales of $700-1,250m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 5.7% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (31.6% in FY ending 2028-04-29) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 31.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-01) to 22.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-04-29 below 28.1% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 31.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-01) to 31.0% over 6 years, then holds. adequate moat: 25% of the excess of current margin 31.7% over the type-typical 25.0% competed away. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-04-29 below the base path 31.6% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 31.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-01) to 36.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 29.8% and margins above 34.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Evidenced source: SerDes/DSP know-how plus system reliability qualified at five hyperscalers, paid for at a steady ~68% non-GAAP gross margin. Not strong: Broadcom, Marvell and Astera Labs are named on every line, Astera is growing faster now, MaxLinear targets 1.6T AECs, and every lane-speed generation is a new design-win contest.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 25.0% is competed away (1.7% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 24.8% against a demonstrated ROIC 96.9% (Ku 9.5% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (cyclical business (semiconductor): the cycle's average return, no persistence premium); demonstrated average: scale-up path (FY2023-FY2026: revenue up every year, operating margin from losses to the window high): mean of the 2 post-breakeven years (17.8%, 96.9%) = 57.4%, not the 4-year mean 19.0% that averages the start-up losses). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 14.8% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-08-01), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 2.6% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 2.6% = min(3-year average capex 6.9%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 2.2306851439092936, type range (0.8, 2.0), base 2.00, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 0.94). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 34.7% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.250 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2023-04-29..2026-05-02; deferred revenue kept at 0.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.00 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 15.0%: 3-year effective 1.1% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 466,869,000 in the first period rising to 466,869,000 (base) of today's cash 466,869,000: about 2.48 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 50% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 0.0% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 0 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 10.00% (risk-free + stage spread); any assumed new money at 10.00% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 297,389,000 earn the risk-free rate 5.00% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 11.00%: table rate 11.00% (risk-free 5.00% + ERP 4.50% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, cyclical +0.50%, weak_customer_concentration +0.25%, weak_competition +0.25%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 10.00% with the expected return on debt 6.00% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 10.00% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 11.00% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 9.50% = E/V x terminal Ke 9.50% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 9.50% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 11.00%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2047-04-29: growth 4.5%, operating margin 22.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 30.0% of NOPAT with ROIC 15.0% (adequate moat, Ku+1pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 9.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 9.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: base terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2047-04-29: growth 5.0%, operating margin 31.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 20.2% of NOPAT with ROIC 24.8% (adequate moat, Ku + 50% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+2pp) (demonstrated average 57.4% over the post-breakeven years of a scale-up path, not the 4-year mean 19.0%); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 9.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 9.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2047-04-29: growth 5.0%, operating margin 36.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 16.0% of NOPAT with ROIC 31.2% (adequate moat, Ku + 71% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+4pp) (demonstrated average 57.4% over the post-breakeven years of a scale-up path, not the 4-year mean 19.0%); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 9.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 9.5%.

assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-10-28: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 495,699,213,080 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 495,699,213,080 (reported year to date 229,692,000,000 (2 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the remaining 0.50 years to 2026-12-31 at the same months a year earlier x year-to-date growth (266,007,213,080)); growth 23.1% vs the last report. The stub 2026-10-28..2026-12-31 runs at 528,038,774,878/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-06-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 3.0 years in base (maturing stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.99% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 21.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 11.8% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 11.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 6.5% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.6% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 16.0% or above 25.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 23.1% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 18.4% for reference): 21.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 11.3% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.4% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 21.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 11.8% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 30.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 17.3% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.4% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 13.5% a year over 10 fiscal years (10.9% after 2.35% expected inflation); 3% of companies with sales of >$50,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 1.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (32.7% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 33.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 26.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 5.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 30.2% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 33.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 31.0% over 5 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 33.1% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 32.1% only up to the type ceiling 40.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 32.7% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 33.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 35.0% over 5 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 5.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 45.0% and margins above 34.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Evidenced sources: scale and intent data in Search plus distribution: referral search share about 90% vs Bing 5.3%; Services margin 40.7% in Q3 2026 (about 42.5% a year earlier ex the EC fine) with a TAC rate of 20.0%; ROIC 28.9% far above the cost of capital. The ad moat holds on level and margin, not on share gains (Meta grows faster). Mechanisms that could break it: the Search judgment's data-sharing and distribution limits and AI-assistant substitution (both unsized).): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 6.3% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30), fading by 20% of its level over 5 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 5.2% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 5.2% = min(3-year average capex 16.1%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.0773250020199843, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 0.43, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.54). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.128 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 1.8% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.04 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 16.0%: 3-year effective 16.0% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(3 months of cash costs, today's cash), 56,334,000,000 in the first period rising to 56,334,000,000 (base) of today's cash 56,334,000,000: about 4.58 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 86.7% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 144,352,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 1.00% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 7.99% (risk-free + 3%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 343,994,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.99% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 9.70%: table rate 9.70% (risk-free 4.99% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:maturing +0.50%, capital_intensity_high +0.50%, weak_governance +0.25%, country_risk +0.64%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.38%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.96% with the expected return on debt 5.99% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 1.00% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 9.70% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 9.20% = E/V x terminal Ke 9.20% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 9.20% (the table without stage:maturing +0.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 9.70%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.label: analyst override: sales_to_capital
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of sales_to_capital: Revenue added per dollar of net reinvestment. Base 0.43 (repair 2026-10-28, review finding ct1): the FY2026 capex guide (195-205bn, reaffirmed on 2026-10-28; 9M 132.0bn) less depreciation of about 30bn is about 170bn of net investment against a revenue step of about 96bn (0.56). Management guided capex to 'increase significantly in 2027' (rp_call_20261028) without a number. At 0.52 the base kept capex near 211bn a year (+5% on the 200bn midpoint), which contradicts that guidance. At 0.43 the base FY2027 revenue step of about 107bn needs about 250bn of growth capex plus maintenance, about 25-30% above the 2026 midpoint, the reviewer's 'at least 20-25% above 200bn'. The same ratio is held through the explicit years: no evidence yet says the 2027 step reverses (the 924bn of purchase commitments are fixed). Bear 0.30: capex does NOT fall with slower revenue (guided, committed: 924bn of purchase commitments), so a bear revenue step of about 53bn rides on roughly the same net investment, on top of 34.1bn of 2026 acquisitions (Wiz, Intersect). Bull 0.8 (own history): FY2023-25 cumulative about 0.94 (revenue +120bn on net capex of about 128bn), i.e. capacity monetises as fast as before the 2026 step-up. New debt, convertible or equity changes claims, dilution and the funding assumption of the thesis.

anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 10,147,000,000, investments 0 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 24,200,000,000 (noncurrent+current; operating leases treated in cash costs; includes 262,000,000 of debt-like claims from inputs), deferred revenue 0 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 871,176,114 at 2026-10-26 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: Filings show the liabilities are customer prepayments or trade payables of an operating business, not funding of a loan book.
assumptions.label: operating classification of a lender-shaped balance sheet
assumptions.rationale: Liabilities are 88% of assets at 2026-09-30 and no cost of revenue is reported: the balance sheet looks like a lender's (deposits or wholesale funding), whatever the industry label. An operating FCFF forecast treats that funding as debt and its spread as operating margin; a residual-income model (book equity, ROE, cost of equity) is the economic route. A reviewer must confirm the operating classification with evidence or reroute.

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 37,571,910,027 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 37,571,910,027 (reported year to date 27,482,000,000 (3 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the remaining 0.25 years to 2026-12-31 at the same months a year earlier x year-to-date growth (10,089,910,027)); growth 14.6% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 40,058,039,537/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 3.0 years in base (maturing stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 11.5% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 8.1% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 8.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 5.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.7% in FY ending 2036-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 9.8% or above 12.8%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 14.6% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 14.8% for reference): 11.5% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 7.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.8% in FY ending 2036-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 11.5% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 8.1% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 14.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 9.4% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.8% in FY ending 2036-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 8.7% a year over 10 fiscal years (6.2% after 2.35% expected inflation); 26% of companies with sales of $12,000-25,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 2.7% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (58.5% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 58.6% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 53.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 5.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 56.0% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 58.6% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 58.0% over 5 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 58.6% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 57.6% only up to the type ceiling 40.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 58.5% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 58.6% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 61.0% over 5 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 5.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 55.0% and margins above 61.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Network effect of two-sided acceptance (3.54bn cards) shared in a duopoly with Visa; evidenced by about 58-61% operating margins for six years and ROIC about 87-98% (forensic screen), incremental ROIC about 120%. The mechanism that stops returns fading is the two-sided network plus regulation-heavy entry; the rent is shared with issuers (rebates) and capped by regulators, not by new networks.): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 1.8% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 20% of its level over 5 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 3.5% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 1.6% = min(3-year average capex 1.6%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 3.6927921623512945, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 1.08, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.08). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 2.9% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 100%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.105 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 0.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.00 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 20.5%: 3-year effective 17.8% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(3 months of cash costs, today's cash), 3,620,795,236 in the first period rising to 7,780,955,978 (base) of today's cash 10,147,000,000: about 8.93 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 90.9% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 24,200,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 4.15% (interest expense / reported debt, latest quarter 2026-09-30 annualized (250,000,000 x 3.97; fiscal year 722,000,000), corroborated by the debt (19,000,000,000 at the fiscal year end -> 23,938,000,000)); any assumed new money at 7.98% (risk-free + 3%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 0 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 8.68%: table rate 8.68% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:maturing +0.50%, country_risk +0.00%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.00%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.14% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 4.15% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 2.8%) = 8.68% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 17,673,795,236 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 632,281,311,950 gives debt weight 2.7% (converged, 2 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal rate 8.18% (one rate for all scenarios, floored at terminal growth + 3 points); each scenario's horizon debt earns its tax shield 0.85% (Kd_promised x tax, at most 3%) as a bridge item D x shield / (rate - g), at most the debt: debt is credited with its tax shield only, never as cheaper capital, so more debt never raises the value; the terminal Ke (not relevered) is the mature table 8.18% (the table without stage:maturing +0.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended); the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 8.68%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.rationale: After 2036-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 53.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 14.9% of NOPAT with ROIC 30.0% (strong moat, 70% of the base ROIC, at least Ku+2pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.2%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.2%.

assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of growth: FY2027-FY2029 from MA's own history: revenue growth 23%, 18%, 13%, 12%, 16% (2021-2025, 2021-2022 a post-COVID travel rebound) and 13% currency-neutral 9M 2026, with a slow fade because the volume line has decelerated (GDV +7%) and rebates take a growing share of gross assessments (51.3% -> 52.6%). Bear fades faster on regulation (routing mandate, cross-border caps) and rail substitution; bull keeps VAS-led growth near 13-14%. Years after the list fade by the engine rule. (evidence pf_revenue_fy2021, pf_revenue_fy2022, pf_revenue_fy2023, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2025, dc_f_nr_g_ytd_cn, dc_f_rebates_share_q3, dc_f_rebates_share_fy25; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.falsifier: The cited evidence is contradicted by a later filing or the override reason no longer holds.
assumptions.label: analyst override: mature_margin
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of mature_margin: GAAP operating margin (litigation and restructuring kept as recurring costs): FY2021 53.4%, FY2025 57.6%, Q3 2026 59.8%, 9M 2026 adjusted 60.8%. Base 58%: FY2025's GAAP level, below the current ~60% that the quarter review flags as a peak run rate, because rebates rise faster than gross assessments and litigation provisions recur. Bear 53%: back to the 2020-2021 level if routing/fee regulation and incentive inflation squeeze the network yield. Bull 61%: today's best adjusted level holds as VAS scales. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_operating_income_fy2021, pf_revenue_fy2021, dc_f_opm_gaap_q3, dc_f_opm_adj_ytd, dc_f_litprov_ytd; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

Share count grew more than 2% a year above the assumed path: current holders own less of every future dollar.
Net debt rose above the planned path by more than 10% of the equity value at analysis: claims ahead of shareholders changed.
Trailing-four-quarter growth is running below the bear-year growth: an early signal before the annual report.
Management changed its own outlook: the forecast anchors may no longer hold.
New debt, convertible or equity changes claims, dilution and the funding assumption of the thesis.
