anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 11,222,000,000, investments 74,352,000,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 3,125,000,000; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 103,591,625,000 (noncurrent+current; operating leases treated in cash costs; includes 19,922,625,000 of debt-like claims from inputs), deferred revenue 0 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 2,556,241,253 at 2026-10-16 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 256,213,000,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 256,213,000,000 (reported year to date 181,713,000,000 (3 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the company's guided midpoint for Q4 FY2026 74,500,000,000 (73,000,000,000-76,000,000,000, issued 2026-10-21; management guidance, not a reported fact); the guided quarter is the last of the fiscal year); growth 27.5% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 295,773,097,826/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 20.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 13.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 6.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.7% in FY ending 2038-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 16.5% or above 23.0%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 27.5% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 24.9% for reference): 20.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 9.9% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.7% in FY ending 2038-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 20.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 26.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 13.9% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 7.0% in FY ending 2038-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 12.8% a year over 10 fiscal years (10.2% after 2.35% expected inflation); 4% of companies with sales of >$50,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 1.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (33.5% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 29.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 30.0% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 37.0% over 6 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 32.9% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 42.2% only up to the type ceiling 45.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 33.5% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 42.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 45.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 44.8% and margins above 40.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Moat source evidenced: network scale (3.64 billion daily people) plus AI ranking that turns it into ad yield; META grew advertising 26% against Google about 11% and Amazon about 11% in Q3 2026. ROIC 28.7% last, 31.4% average (auto.json forensic), well above the 8% reference; incremental ROIC fell to 14.9% as capex rises, so the excess return is fading toward the cost of capital at the margin.): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 11.2% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 9.3% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 9.3% = min(3-year average capex 25.8%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.0790927930002303, type range (0.3, 1.0), base 0.70, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.28). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.028 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 0.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.00 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 16.0%: 3-year effective 20.6% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 11,222,000,000 in the first period rising to 11,222,000,000 (base) of today's cash 11,222,000,000: about 4.39 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 60.1% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 103,591,625,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 1.12% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 74,352,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 10.76%: table rate 10.76% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, capital_intensity_high +0.50%, weak_governance +0.25%, country_risk +0.52%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.20%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.80% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 1.12% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 1.4%) = 10.76% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 29,239,625,000 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 2,120,727,282,150 gives debt weight 1.4% (converged, 5 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 9.21% = E/V x terminal Ke 9.26% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 9.26% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 10.76%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.

assumptions.rationale: After 2038-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 29.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 16.1% of NOPAT with ROIC 27.9% (strong moat, 70% of the base ROIC, at least Ku+2pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 9.3%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 9.2%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.

assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of mature_margin: Operating margin after SBC (SBC is inside META's GAAP costs). Own history: 24.8% (2022 trough), 34.7% (2023), 42.2% (2024 peak), 41.4% (2025); FY2026 implied about 31% reported and about 35% ex the 9.89B AG charge (expense guide 175-179B on about 256B revenue). Base 37%: partial recovery as the Reality Labs loss narrows to about 15B in 2027 (about +1.5 points) and capex growth slows, but depreciation of a 250B+ asset base and AI token costs keep it below the 2024-25 level. Bull 42%: back to the 2024 peak as AI products monetize the installed compute. Bear 30%: depreciation, cloud capacity and recurring legal costs keep expense growth above revenue (Q3 2026 ex-charge 35%, FoA margin down 22 points y/y). Repair: bear 29% at maturity (was 30%) to match the bear cash-cost path (the explicit years go to 26% in 2029, toward the 2022 trough); the yearly margin path is now set by cash_cost_ratio, starting ex the 12.29B legal charges. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2022, pf_revenue_fy2022, pf_operating_income_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_operating_income_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2025, dc_g_total_expenses_fy2026, dc_legal_charge_ag_q3_2026, dc_g_reality_labs_loss_fy2027, nm_operating_income_ex_legal_q_2026_09_30; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

values.meaning: Conditional value per share at each date (valuation.value_company); not a price forecast.

price_for_hurdle.formula: base value with cost of equity = required return (terminal WACC moved by the equity weight 1 - w, Harris-Pringle); the base IRR at this price equals the required return
price_for_hurdle.label: value at your required return

verdict_detail.reason: strong business; base IRR 12.02% >= required return 10.76% (index 9.18% + 1.58pp premium, floored at the model cost of equity); bear-case loss 37% (at your required return) within the 40% tolerance for strong quality; conditional on SBC settled in new shares: bear: part of SBC settled in 77,592,457 new shares at the issue-price rule (min(quote, scenario value per share right after the issue))
what_would_change_it: price above 830 (base IRR would fall below the required return)

anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 20,281,000,000, investments 82,036,000,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 106,454,000,000 (noncurrent+current; operating leases treated in cash costs; includes 70,973,000,000 of debt-like claims from inputs), deferred revenue 69,563,000,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 7,426,194,552 at 2026-10-22 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2027-06-30 revenue differs from 395,541,857,418 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2027-06-30 revenue 395,541,857,418 (reported year to date 92,279,000,000 (1 reported quarter(s) after 2026-06-30) + the company's guided midpoint for Q2 FY2027 96,550,000,000 (96,000,000,000-97,100,000,000, issued 2026-10-28; management guidance, not a reported fact) + the remaining 2 quarter(s) 101,018,677,055, 105,694,180,363 at the guided quarter's own sequential growth 4.6% (guide / the last reported quarter 92,279,000,000) compounded); growth 19.2% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2027-06-30 runs at 405,739,042,755/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2027-06-30.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-06-30 above 17.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 7.4% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 8.0% in FY ending 2028-06-30, 5.4% in FY ending 2032-06-30, 4.6% in FY ending 2039-06-30; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-06-30 below 12.5% or above 20.0%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 19.2% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 17.9% for reference): 17.0% in FY ending 2028-06-30, 8.9% in FY ending 2032-06-30, 5.5% in FY ending 2039-06-30; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-06-30 below 17.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 7.4% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 23.0% in FY ending 2028-06-30, 12.7% in FY ending 2032-06-30, 6.7% in FY ending 2039-06-30; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 10.9% a year over 10 fiscal years (8.3% after 2.35% expected inflation); 10% of companies with sales of >$50,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 1.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (46.6% in FY ending 2028-06-30) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 47.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 38.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-06-30 below 43.1% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 47.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 44.0% over 6 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 47.1% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 46.8% only up to the type ceiling 45.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-06-30 below the base path 46.6% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 47.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 48.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 45.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 27.0% and margins above 47.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Sources evidenced: an installed enterprise base (Microsoft 365 seats +6% in FY2026 with rising revenue per user) and scale in cloud. Operating margin 46.8% in FY2026 vs whole-company 32.0% Alphabet, 30.6% Oracle, 11.2% Amazon; ROIC 31% last year (average 34%) against an 8% cost-of-capital reference. Segment margins of the competitors not retrieved.): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 3.6% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 10.3% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 10.3% = min(3-year average capex 25.3%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 0.5056436073550308, type range (0.3, 1.0), base 0.55, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 0.62). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.056 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2023-06-30..2026-06-30; deferred revenue kept at 17.1% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.34 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 20.0%: 3-year effective 18.5% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 20,281,000,000 in the first period rising to 20,281,000,000 (base) of today's cash 20,281,000,000: about 2.73 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 61.2% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 106,454,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 2.87% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 82,036,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 10.22%: table rate 10.22% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, capital_intensity_high +0.50%, weak_customer_concentration +0.25%, country_risk +0.00%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.21%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.38% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 2.87% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.7%) = 10.22% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 24,418,000,000 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 3,509,024,850,973 gives debt weight 0.7% (converged, 4 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 8.70% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.72% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.72% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 10.22%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value

assumptions.label: analyst override: sales_to_capital
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of sales_to_capital: Lease-inclusive basis, consistent with the finance-lease liabilities deducted as debt: incremental revenue / (cash capex + finance-lease ROU additions from the 10-K/10-Q lease note - D&A). FY2024-FY2026: 119.9B / 210.2B = 0.57; FY2026 0.47 (50.1B / 106.3B), FY2025 0.58, FY2024 0.81. Base 0.55: near the three-year figure, slightly below it because capex keeps rising (Q1 FY2027 cash PP&E 39.4B plus 5.2B finance leases; CY2026 capex guided ~175B). Bear 0.42: below the FY2026 low of 0.47 (capex above 50B a quarter while growth slows). Bull 0.75: capex flattens as the fleet fills and conversion moves back toward FY2024 (0.81). Future datacenter leases shift to operating leases (outside capex, inside operating costs), and the 364.6B of leases not yet commenced are outside this capital base: their cost is carried in the margin lever, not here. (evidence pf_revenue_fy2023, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2026, pf_capex_fy2024, pf_capex_fy2025, pf_capex_fy2026, pf_d_and_a_fy2024, pf_d_and_a_fy2025, pf_d_and_a_fy2026, rf_fin_lease_rou_fy2024, rf_fin_lease_rou_fy2025, rf_fin_lease_rou_fy2026, rf_fin_lease_rou_q1fy27, dc_capex_cash_q1fy27, rf_g_capex_cy26; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

triggers.why: Current fiscal year revenue more than 3% below its anchor (the revenue_current_fy falsifier): every scenario grows from too high a starting revenue.

triggers.formula: lowest scenario operating margin of the stub period that completes the current fiscal year - margin tolerance
triggers.why: Current fiscal year operating margin below the lowest margin any scenario starts from, beyond definition noise: every margin path starts too high.

Operating margin below the bear case beyond definition noise: unit economics or pricing power are weaker than the worst case assumed.

anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 2,393,000,000, investments 4,568,000,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 7,524,000,000 (tagged_total; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 7,733,000,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 1,038,000,000 at 2026-09-30 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: single_source.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 16,222,133,265 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 16,222,133,265 (reported year to date 11,863,000,000 (3 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the remaining 0.25 years to 2026-12-31 at the same months a year earlier x year-to-date growth (4,359,133,265)); growth 22.2% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 17,306,232,880/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 5.0 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 19.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 13.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 7.9% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.7% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 16.0% or above 20.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 22.2% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 21.9% for reference): 19.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 13.0% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.5% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 19.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 22.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 16.4% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 8.5% in FY ending 2043-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 14.4% a year over 10 fiscal years (11.7% after 2.35% expected inflation); 7% of companies with sales of $7,000-12,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 3.2% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (12.4% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 9.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 14.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 8.9% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 9.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 26.0% over 6 years, then holds. below type-typical: base closes 70% of the gap from 9.7% to 25.0% (not below the best of 3 years 13.7%). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 12.4% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 9.7% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 30.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 27.0% and margins above 29.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Evidenced moat source is switching costs on the installed workflow base (98% renewal) plus faster growth than Salesforce and Workday; but GAAP ROIC was about 14% last year and about 9% on average against an 8% reference, close to the cost of capital once stock compensation is counted, the 10-K describes low barriers to entry, and goodwill rose to about $10bn in 2026, which will weigh on returns on capital. Strong cash economics (FCF margin above 30% for six years) do not yet show up as high GAAP returns.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 25.0% is competed away (0.0% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 22.0% against a demonstrated ROIC 50.1% (Ku 8.2% + 60% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (demonstrated ROIC 50.1% vs hurdle 8.2% (excess 1.00); ROIC variation 38% over 5 years (stability 0.40); gross margin 77.5%, range 2.1% over 5 years (margin 1.00))). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 15.1% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 5.6% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 5.6% = min(3-year average capex 7.3%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.4099088572096283, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 1.95, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.00). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 23.6% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.161 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 44.7% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.89 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 15.0%: 3-year effective 2.1% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 2,393,000,000 in the first period rising to 2,393,000,000 (base) of today's cash 2,393,000,000: about 2.31 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 50% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 28.7% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 7,524,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 1.00% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 4,568,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 9.70%: table rate 9.70% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, country_risk +0.37%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.35%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.96% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 1.00% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 1.9%) = 9.70% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 2,956,000,000 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 153,399,052,474 gives debt weight 1.9% (converged, 4 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 8.15% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.20% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.20% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 9.70%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2043-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 14.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 29.9% of NOPAT with ROIC 15.0% (adequate moat, Ku+1pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.2%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.2%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2043-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 30.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 15.3% of NOPAT with ROIC 32.6% (adequate moat, Ku + 77% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+4pp) (persistence lifted from the 71% floor by a durable realized ROIC: demonstrated ROIC 50.1% vs hurdle 8.2% (excess 1.00); ROIC variation 38% over 5 years (stability 0.40); gross margin 77.5%, range 2.1% over 5 years (margin 1.00)); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.2%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.2%.

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows common equity more than 2% different.
assumptions.label: opening book equity
assumptions.rationale: common book equity 13,063,221,000 at 2026-06-30 (stockholders' equity less preferred stock); deposits, float and reserves are operating funding inside it, not debt (inputs.bank_drivers.opening, a later filing than the FactBook's 2025-12-31: Q2 2026 6-K IFRS statement of financial position at 2026-06-30: equity attributable to shareholders of the parent 13,249,670k, less other comprehensive income 186,449k (AOCI, mostly currency translation; it was -184,300k at 2025-12-31) = 13,063,221k common book on the FactBook basis (no preferred stock). Shares: 20-F count at 2026-03-01 (3,837,998,543 Class A + 1,022,600,698 Class B = 4,860,599,241) less the 40,659,600 Class A shares held in treasury at 2026-06-30 (none at 2025-12-31; repurchased under the US$1.0bn program) = 4,819,939,641. Share issuance from employee awards after 2026-03-01 is not in this count (small; the next cover count will tell), and any repurchase before 2026-03-01 would be counted twice (the 6-K does not date them).)

assumptions.falsifier: The share count at as_of differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: point-in-time common shares 4,819,939,641; constant over the forecast (buybacks are treated like dividends)

assumptions.falsifier: Reported profit or book equity for these years differs.
assumptions.label: return on equity history
assumptions.rationale: ROE = profit to common / average common equity (net income available to common stockholders (as reported)); trailing 30.3% (net income available to common, trailing twelve months), median 28.1% and lower quartile 18.2% over 3 fiscal years; the path starts at 29.2% (median of the trailing twelve months and the last three fiscal years); ROE above the 11.2% cost of equity in 3 of 3 years

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the bear path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: bear ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (own_history): ROE 21.0% to 15.0% by year 5, 11.5% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 13.0% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 26.0%: Bear mechanisms from review/counter.json, each sized from company evidence: (1) credit: Stage 2 rose 10.1% -> 11.9% of gross, NPL 90+ 6.9% (seven-quarter high) and Brazil household defaults at a record 8.1%; cost of risk normalizes up as loan growth slows and IFRS 9 front-loading stops masking losses, taking ROE from the tax-normalized 26-27% to 21% at the start and to 15% by year 5, below Nu's own FY2023 18% level; (2) tax: the 2026 deferred-tax benefit does not recur and CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 (about 1-2 points of ROE); (3) BRL: about 91% of revenue is Brazilian and the real fell about 10% intraday after the 2026-10-25 election, so USD book growth carries translation losses beside retained profit: start 13% (vs 19% base), within retention 21% x (1 - 26%) = 15.5%, fading; (4) capital: CET1 11.9% and falling forces slower RWA growth. Payout floor stays the evidenced 26% buyback share (H1 2026).; terminal: Terminal ROE 11.5% is set at about the 11.2% cost of equity: in the bear the excess return is competed and taxed away (CSLL 20% from 2028, BCB limits on unsolicited credit marketing from 2027); the half point left is the reported cost-to-serve advantage only.

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the base path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: base ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (own_history): ROE 27.0% to 25.0% by year 5, 16.0% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 19.0% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 26.0%: ROE: tax-normalized own run rate. H1 2026 net income 1,932.5m was booked at an 11.8% tax rate (Q2 14.2% with a one-off deferred-tax benefit) against 25.8% in FY2025 (income tax 996.7m on pretax 3,868.4m); at the FY2025 rate H1 profit is about 1.63bn, about 3.25bn a year, about 26.5% on average H1 parent equity (11.29bn -> 13.25bn); FY2024 28.1% and FY2025 30.3% on average equity (reported). Start 27%, year 5 25% after CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 (about 1-2 points). Book growth: own common equity grew about 26%/yr 2021-25, 33%/yr 2023-25 and 13.8% in H1 2026 alone ex-AOCI (about 29% annualized); the start is held at 19% (below that history) because the Brazilian conglomerate's CET1 fell 13.0% -> 11.9% in six months as RWA grew 14.7% vs CET1 capital +5.4% (excess over the minimum 1.85bn): growth is limited by the capital the business retains, fading to terminal growth. Payout floor 26% = H1 2026 buybacks 500.4m / net income 1,932.5m (US$1.0bn program to June 2027, 499.6m left; no dividend).; terminal: Terminal ROE 16% stays above the 11.2% cost of equity because Nu's own lowest post-breakeven ROE was about 18% (FY2023: net income 1,030.5m on average parent equity about 5.65bn) and its cost-to-serve / efficiency advantage is reported every quarter (efficiency ratio in the Q2 2026 release); the 16% sits two points below that own low to allow for the CSLL rise and competition, not a peer number.

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the bull path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: bull ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (own_history): ROE 30.0% to 31.0% by year 5, 20.0% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 22.0% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 26.0%: ROE: start 30% (reported FY2025 30.3% on average equity; H1 2026 about 31.5% reported, 26.5% tax-normalized, so the bull assumes the credit models keep cost of risk flat while ARPAC keeps rising +37% y/y), year 5 31% as Mexico (revenue +79% y/y in Q2 2026) matures. Book growth start 22% within retention 30% x (1 - 26%) = 22.2%, below the own 2023-25 26-33%/yr, capped by the CET1 room (11.9%, excess 1.85bn). Payout floor 26% = H1 2026 buyback share.; terminal: Terminal ROE 20% above the 11.2% cost of equity: in the bull Nu keeps its reported ROE (FY2025 30% on average equity, Q2 2026 33% reported) through scale in Brazil and the Mexico bank license (CNBV authorization 2026-07-09, 15.8m customers, loan-to-deposit 35% with room to lend), so the terminal is set at its own 2024-25 level less a third for tax and competition.

assumptions.falsifier: Distributions over the next two years differ from this share of profit by more than 20 points.
assumptions.label: distributions
assumptions.rationale: no distribution history: 50% assumed; book grows by retained profit (clean surplus), at most the growth the business can use: the engine cap 8.0% (its own five-year common-equity growth 91.5% is above it) (bounded 3.0%-8.0%) fading to terminal growth, so profit beyond that need is paid out (payout = max(history, 1 - book growth / ROE)); inputs.bank_drivers sets the start growth and the payout floor in ['bear', 'base', 'bull']

assumptions.falsifier: The terminal ROE is not sustainable at the business's regulatory capital and competitive position.
assumptions.label: terminal growth and ROE
assumptions.rationale: terminal growth = min(risk-free, 8% (the valuation contract's bound), ROE x retention, ROE - 0.1pp, Ke - 0.5pp), at least 0 (perpetual growth at the risk-free rate: the convention of the implied equity risk premium); terminal value = book x (ROE - g) / (Ke - g)

assumptions.falsifier: A dated market-implied cost of equity for comparable banks or insurers differs by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: cost of equity
assumptions.rationale: risk-free + equity risk premium + stage add-on + balance-sheet add-on; no relevering (deposits and float are operating funding)

assumptions.falsifier: CET1 (or solvency) ratios fall below requirements plus buffers on this payout.
assumptions.label: regulatory capital
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers.regulatory_capital: risk-weighted assets 35,710,139,000 at 2026-06-30, growing with each scenario's book growth path; common book must stay at or above 10.5% of them (common book is a proxy: CET1 deducts goodwill and intangibles): Q2 2026 6-K capital note, Nu Prudential Conglomerate (Brazil): RWA 35,710,139k; minimum capital required 3,749,565k = 10.5% of RWA (the requirement with the conservation buffer, as the filing computes it); CET1 4,262,877k = 11.9% (13.0% at 2025-12-31), excess margin 1,848,040k. Nu Holdings itself has no regulatory capital requirement; CET1 sits in the regulated Brazilian (and Mexican, 14.9% vs 10.5%; Colombian, 15.3% vs 10.5%) entities, so the consolidated common book used here is only a PROXY: it is about three times the conglomerate's CET1, so the engine's check on it is loose and the real binding limit is the conglomerate's 11.9% CET1, which is why book growth starts below Nu's own history.

assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-08-31: cash 36,369,000,000, investments 708,000,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 130,291,000,000 (tagged_plus_current; operating leases treated in cash costs; includes 4,954,000,000 of debt-like claims from inputs), deferred revenue 30,789,000,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 3,023,736,000 at 2026-09-07 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-08-31 and as_of 2026-10-29: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2027-05-31 revenue differs from 90,000,000,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2027-05-31 revenue 90,000,000,000 (FY2027 revenue: company guidance midpoint 90,000,000,000 (90,000,000,000-90,000,000,000, issued 2026-09-10); FY2027 revenue guidance 'at least $90B' (raised from $85B in Mar-2026, held on 2026-09-10); Q1 FY27 reported $19.345B and Q2 guided +30-34% ($20.9-21.5B). The guide is a floor and the revenue track record is a small beat (ratio 1.008 over 6 periods), but no guidance item covers only the unreported Q2-Q4 remainder, so no adjustment; attributed consensus $90.4B (ex_c_rev_fy27) is a cross-check only. (evidence rp_g_fy27_rev, web:pf_rel_20260910_1, rp_f_rev_q1fy27, rp_g_q2fy27_rev; source tier guidance)); growth 33.6% vs the last report. The stub 2026-10-29..2027-05-31 runs at 94,530,178,571/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-08-31 to 2027-05-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (maturing stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.99% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-05-31 above 44.4% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 9.6% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 15.0% in FY ending 2028-05-31, 7.1% in FY ending 2032-05-31, 4.5% in FY ending 2044-05-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2028-05-31 below 29.7% or above 46.2%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth

assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 9.6% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 48.0% in FY ending 2028-05-31, 23.3% in FY ending 2032-05-31, 6.4% in FY ending 2044-05-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 22.3% a year over 10 fiscal years (19.5% after 2.35% expected inflation); 0% of companies with sales of >$25,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 1.8% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (31.7% in FY ending 2028-05-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-31) to 25.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 5.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-05-31 below 29.2% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-31) to 30.0% over 5 years, then holds. adequate moat: 25% of the excess of current margin 32.1% over the type-typical 30.0% competed away. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2028-05-31 below the base path 31.7% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 32.1% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-08-31) to 35.0% over 5 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 5.0%, capped at the type ceiling 45.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 18.0% and margins above 33.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Strong in the database and support base (renewed by substantially all customers; the database is sold inside AWS, Azure and Google Cloud); no evidenced moat in OCI against AWS, Azure and Google Cloud beyond available capacity and won contracts.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 30.0% is competed away (0.5% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 13.0% against a demonstrated ROIC 14.9% (Ku 9.2% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (demonstrated ROIC 14.9% vs hurdle 9.2% (excess 0.05); ROIC variation 87% over 5 years (stability 0.00); operating margin 30.6%, range 5.1% over 5 years (no cost of revenue reported) (margin 0.59))). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 6.7% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-08-31), fading by 20% of its level over 5 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 11.3% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 11.3% = min(3-year average capex 44.2%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 0.29602980200040824, type range (0.3, 1.0), base 0.50, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 0.51). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio -0.300 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2023-05-31..2026-05-31; deferred revenue kept at 32.6% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.65 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 15.0%: 3-year effective 12.0% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(3 months of cash costs, today's cash), 11,781,791,640 in the first period rising to 36,369,000,000 (base) of today's cash 36,369,000,000: about 12.03 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = n/a of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 130,291,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 3.53% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 7.99% (risk-free + 3%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 708,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.99% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 10.69%: table rate 10.69% (risk-free 4.99% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:maturing +0.50%, capital_intensity_high +0.50%, needs_external_funding +1.00%, weak_customer_concentration +0.25%, weak_competition +0.25%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.75% with the expected return on debt 5.99% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 3.53% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 16.2%) = 10.69% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 104,995,791,640 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 646,290,837,062 gives debt weight 14.0% (converged, 8 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price (per-share values of base, bull still depend on the quote: new shares are issued at the quote below their own value). Terminal WACC 8.67% = E/V x terminal Ke 9.19% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 9.19% (the table without stage:maturing +0.50%, needs_external_funding +1.00%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 10.69%. External-funding add-on applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.
