anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-06-30: cash 2,030,047,000, investments 7,379,052,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 0 (noncurrent+current; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 613,159,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 2,403,058,480 at 2026-07-27 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-06-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 8,331,597,490 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 8,331,597,490 (FY2026 revenue: company guidance midpoint 8,154,000,000 (8,150,000,000-8,158,000,000, issued 2026-08-03) + (track-record ratio 1.0821 - 1) x the Q3 2026 guided midpoint 2,162,000,000 = 8,331,597,490; FY2026 guide 8.150-8.158B raised on 2026-08-03; the company beat its revenue guide in 8 of 8 recorded periods (ratio 1.082), so the ratio is applied to the Q3 guide (the only guided unreported item); the implied Q4 (about 2.42B) is left unadjusted, which keeps the estimate on the cautious side. (evidence dc_g_fy_rev, dc_g_q3_rev, web:pf_rel_20260803_1; source tier guidance)); growth 86.2% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 9,455,906,611/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-06-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 45.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 14.3% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 25.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 9.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.5% in FY ending 2046-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 35.0% or above 55.0%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 86.2% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 66.8% for reference): 45.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 18.2% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.2% in FY ending 2046-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 45.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 14.3% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 65.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 30.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.0% in FY ending 2046-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 26.6% a year over 10 fiscal years (23.7% after 2.35% expected inflation); 1% of companies with sales of $3,000-4,500m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 4.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (43.2% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 42.8% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 36.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 39.7% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 42.8% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 45.0% over 6 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 42.8% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 31.6% only up to the type ceiling 40.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 43.2% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 42.8% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 50.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 18.4% and margins above 48.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Evidenced source: embedded deployment and expansion inside existing customers (NDR 157%, top-20 average $124M TTM, +67%), with 82% gross margin and 32% GAAP operating margin vs Snowflake (-31% op margin) and C3.ai (-199%). Duration is not proven: the 10-K says in-house builds are the main alternative.): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 13.6% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 0.6% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 0.6% = min(3-year average capex 0.6%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 9.224030239720864, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 5.00, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 0.35). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.319 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 6.5% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.13 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 15.0%: 3-year effective 2.7% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 1,356,753,712 in the first period rising to 2,030,047,000 (base) of today's cash 2,030,047,000: about 0.84 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 50% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 3.5% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 0 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 9.98% (risk-free + stage spread); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 7,379,052,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 9.93%: table rate 9.93% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, weak_governance +0.25%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.14% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 9.98% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 9.93% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 8.43% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.43% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.43% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 9.93%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2046-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 36.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 43.0% of NOPAT with ROIC 10.4% (strong moat, 70% of the base ROIC, at least Ku+2pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.4%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: base terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2046-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 45.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 37.1% of NOPAT with ROIC 13.4% (strong moat, returns stay above the cost of capital: max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp), capped at 40%; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.4%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2046-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 50.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 30.9% of NOPAT with ROIC 16.1% (strong moat, 120% of the base ROIC, capped at 45%; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.4%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: A dated consensus becomes available and differs from the base first-year revenue by more than 10%.
assumptions.label: consensus comparison
assumptions.rationale: The FactBook carries no revenue consensus at as_of (not retrieved or not stored); nothing is fabricated. Growth is anchored on trailing growth instead.

assumptions.falsifier: The cited evidence is contradicted by a later filing or the override reason no longer holds.
assumptions.label: analyst override: growth_anchor
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of growth_anchor: No FY2027 guidance. The FY2026 guide implies Q4 2026 revenue of about 2.42B (8.154B less Q1 1.633B, Q2 1.935B, Q3 guide 2.162B), so the Q4 run rate alone is about 9.7B, +16-19% over FY2026 with zero further sequential growth. Sequential growth was 16% (Q1) and 19% (Q2); base = sequential growth slowing to about 8% a quarter in 2027 (about 12B, +45%), backed by total remaining deal value 13.1B (+83% y/y), U.S. commercial TCV 2.13B in Q2 (+153%) and NDR 157%. Bear = sequential growth falls to about 2-3% a quarter (government timing, deal slippage): about +25%, close to the exit run rate. Bull = sequential growth near 12% a quarter, as in the U.S. commercial TCV trend: about +65%. Attributed consensus (12.36B, +50%, not citable until 2026-11-03) is a cross-check only. (evidence dc_g_fy_rev, dc_g_q3_rev, pf_revenue_q_2026_06_30, pf_revenue_q_2026_03_31, dc_k_total_rdv, dc_k_usc_tcv, dc_k_ndr, dc_f_rpo; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 1,357,583,000, investments 1,675,849,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 0 (none_tagged; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 38,787,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 193,093,731 at 2026-10-28 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 3,378,273,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 3,378,273,000 (reported year to date 2,363,273,000 (3 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the company's guided midpoint for Q4 FY2026 1,015,000,000 (1,000,000,000-1,030,000,000, issued 2026-10-29; management guidance, not a reported fact); the guided quarter is the last of the fiscal year); growth 53.4% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 4,029,660,326/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 2.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 25.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 10.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 4.4% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 2.6% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 2.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 17.5% or above 30.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the current fiscal year's growth 53.4% (year-to-date reports, see revenue_current_fy; trailing growth 59.6% for reference): 25.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 11.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 25.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 36.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 18.2% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.5% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 16.8% a year over 10 fiscal years (14.1% after 2.35% expected inflation); 9% of companies with sales of $1,250-2,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 5.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (30.2% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 29.4% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 25.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 26.7% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 29.4% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 34.0% over 6 years, then holds. adequate moat: 25% of the excess of current margin 29.4% over the type-typical 25.0% competed away. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 30.2% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 29.4% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 40.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 100.0% and margins above 37.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Moat source evidenced: a unique user-generated, topic-organised corpus and community network (91.5% gross margin, above META 82%, PINS 80%). Not strong: user acquisition depends on GOOGL search referrals that are falling, and logged-in DAUq grew only 6.6% y/y (53.5M vs 50.2M); the same AI products from GOOGL/META/OpenAI can summarise the content without the visit.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 25.0% is competed away (1.1% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 95.0% against a demonstrated ROIC 115.5% (Ku 8.0% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (ROIC record under 5 years)). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 12.5% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 0.7% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 0.7% = min(3-year average capex 0.7%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.1902558677532231, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 3.58, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 3.58). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.4% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 100%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.235 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2023-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 1.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.02 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 22.0%: 3-year effective -0.2% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 770,870,399 in the first period rising to 1,357,583,000 (base) of today's cash 1,357,583,000: about 7.03 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 50% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 0.0% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 0 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 9.98% (risk-free + stage spread); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 1,675,849,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 9.36%: table rate 9.36% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, country_risk +0.00%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.32%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.68% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 9.98% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 9.36% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 7.98% = E/V x terminal Ke 7.86% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 7.86% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 9.36%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of terminal_roic: One capital intensity per scenario, from Reddit's operating invested capital (equity less cash and securities; the cash pile is not operating capital): FY2024 290M on revenue 1,300M, FY2025 452M on 2,203M, Q3 2026 580M (incl. 31M leases) on TTM 3,089M; incremental sales-to-capital 5.6 (2024-25) and 9.2 (2025-TTM); receivables are 23.6% of TTM revenue (receivables-only bound about 4.2); capex 0.2-0.3% of revenue. assumptions.label: analyst override: terminal_growth
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of terminal_growth: Bear only (base and bull stay on the engine rule). The bear is a shrinking audience: search referrals down more than 1M a week in October, US logged-out DAUq down y/y (28.5M to 27.3M), management's warned low-double-digit Q4 fall from 130M total DAUq; logged-out users are 59% of DAUq but under 20% of monetization. A business whose audience shrinks does not grow with nominal GDP forever: after 2041 the bear grows at about inflation (2.5%, no real growth). Multiple test: at the engine's 4.5% the bear's computed forward multiple was 21-22x, above today's ~13x forward (consensus FY2027 EPS) and above the own-history trailing low of 18.7x; this lever brings it inside that range. (evidence dc_search_referral_drop, dc_lo_us, dc_lo_us_py, dc_lo_g, dc_dauq_g, web:dc_call_20261029, web:pf_rel_20261029_2; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.rationale: point-in-time common shares 1,291,570,324; constant over the forecast (buybacks are treated like dividends)

assumptions.falsifier: Reported profit or book equity for these years differs.
assumptions.label: return on equity history
assumptions.rationale: ROE = profit to common / average common equity (net income available to common stockholders (as reported)); trailing 7.1% (net income available to common, trailing twelve months), median -6.5% and lower quartile -7.5% over 5 fiscal years; the path starts at 6.4% (median of the trailing twelve months and the last three fiscal years); ROE above the 11.2% cost of equity in 0 of 5 years

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the bear path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: bear ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (own_history): ROE 6.0% to 8.5% by year 5, 8.5% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 5.0% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 0.0%: Start 6%: back to the FY2025 ROE of 5.7%. Mechanisms, sized from SoFi's own filings: (1) fair value - the remaining loan premium is about $1.4bn and a +100bp move cost $1,040.8m before hedges (June 2026 10-Q); losing about half of the premium after tax is about 5% of book; (2) credit - the personal-loan default assumption already rose 4.57% to 5.10%, and an all-in NCO back at the 4.4% of late 2025 on about $31bn of personal loans costs about $300m a year pre-tax; (3) funding/capital - CET1 fell 22.8% to 16.9% in three quarters with RWA +68%, so growth is cut to what retained profit funds (book growth 5%) or new equity is issued below today's price. ROE recovers only to 8.5%, below the cost of equity, also at the terminal.

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the base path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: base ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (guidance): ROE 9.5% to 12.5% by year 5, 11.5% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 9.5% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 0.0%: Start 9.5%: Q3 2026 annualised ROE 8.6% (ROTE 10%), normalised upward for the $10.9m after-tax servicing-rights fair-value charge and toward the FY2027 guide (net income $1.28bn on an average book of about $12.4bn = about 10.3%, computed). Year 5 12.5%: the 2025-2028 EPS CAGR target of 38-42% and the EBITDA margin rising to 35% imply ROE of about 10.5-11% in 2028 (computed); continuing operating leverage (net income margin from about 17% in 2026 to 20% in 2027) takes it to about 12.5% by 2031. Book growth 9.5% = all profit retained (payout 0); the engine keeps shares constant at the point-in-time count, and SBC (about $290m a year) is a cost inside GAAP net income, so dilution from awards is charged. Past raises are in the opening share count.; terminal: A deposit franchise of 17.1m members funding loans at 1.45pp below warehouse funding, products per member rising (1.56) and a NIM guided above 5%: a modest edge of about 0.3pp over the cost of equity is kept, far below today's lending spreads.

assumptions.falsifier: ROE over the next two fiscal years differs from the bull path by more than 3 points.
assumptions.label: bull ROE path
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers (guidance): ROE 10.0% to 16.0% by year 5, 13.5% terminal (cost of equity 11.2%); book growth 10.0% fading to terminal growth by year 10; payout at least 0.0%: Start 10%: the FY2027 guide (net income $1.28bn, about 10.3% on average book, computed) reached early, consistent with EBITDA beats of 13-23% against guidance. Year 5 16% (ROTE about 18%): the top of the 38-42% EPS CAGR target to 2028 sustained by fee revenue (42% of revenue) growing faster than the capital-consuming loan book, NIM held above the guided 5% floor and marketing growing slower than revenue. Book growth 10% = all profit retained.; terminal: A national digital bank with a cheap deposit base (1.45pp below warehouse funding), 42% fee-based revenue that needs little capital and products per member rising: part of the excess return survives competition (Ally, Capital One, Nu) at about 2pp over the cost of equity.

assumptions.falsifier: Distributions over the next two years differ from this share of profit by more than 20 points.
assumptions.label: distributions
assumptions.rationale: no distribution history: 50% assumed; book grows by retained profit (clean surplus), at most the growth the business can use: the engine cap 8.0% (its own five-year common-equity growth 21.4% is above it) (bounded 3.0%-8.0%) fading to terminal growth, so profit beyond that need is paid out (payout = max(history, 1 - book growth / ROE)); inputs.bank_drivers sets the start growth and the payout floor in ['bear', 'base', 'bull']

assumptions.falsifier: The terminal ROE is not sustainable at the business's regulatory capital and competitive position.
assumptions.label: terminal growth and ROE
assumptions.rationale: terminal growth = min(risk-free, 8% (the valuation contract's bound), ROE x retention, ROE - 0.1pp, Ke - 0.5pp), at least 0 (perpetual growth at the risk-free rate: the convention of the implied equity risk premium); terminal value = book x (ROE - g) / (Ke - g)

assumptions.falsifier: A dated market-implied cost of equity for comparable banks or insurers differs by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: cost of equity
assumptions.rationale: risk-free + equity risk premium + stage add-on + balance-sheet add-on; no relevering (deposits and float are operating funding)

assumptions.falsifier: CET1 (or solvency) ratios fall below requirements plus buffers on this payout.
assumptions.label: regulatory capital
assumptions.rationale: inputs.bank_drivers.regulatory_capital: risk-weighted assets 48,682,417,000 at 2026-06-30, growing with each scenario's book growth path; common book must stay at or above 7.0% of them (common book is a proxy: CET1 deducts goodwill and intangibles): SoFi Technologies risk-weighted assets $48.68bn at June 30, 2026 and the CET1 requirement of 7.0% including the 2.5% capital conservation buffer, from the 10-Q capital table. The Q3 release shows RWA already at $56.24bn (Sep 30, 2026; CET1 16.9%), so this filing figure understates the current requirement by about 15%.

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-09-30: cash 17,853,000,000, investments 27,594,000,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 9,267,000,000 (tagged_plus_current; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 8,787,000,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 3,952,757,946 at 2026-10-15 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-09-30 and as_of 2026-10-27: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 106,683,426,236 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 106,683,426,236 (reported year to date 78,669,000,000 (3 reported quarter(s) after 2025-12-31) + the remaining 0.25 years to 2026-12-31 at the same months a year earlier x year-to-date growth (28,014,426,236)); growth 12.5% vs the last report. The stub 2026-10-27..2026-12-31 runs at 111,220,317,204/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-09-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 3.0 years in base (mature stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 5.00% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 9.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: -3.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 2.1% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 3.0% or above 14.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the long-run like-for-like growth 24.6% (5-year CAGR without acquisition steps, else 3-year), not the current fiscal year's 12.5%: a cyclical business's change this year is the cycle, not a trend: 9.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 6.6% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.2% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 9.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 20.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 12.4% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.2% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 7.4% a year over 10 fiscal years (5.0% after 2.35% expected inflation); 21% of companies with sales of >$50,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 1.1% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (4.8% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 3.3% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 5.0% over 3 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 4.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 2.8% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 3.3% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 9.0% over 4 years, then holds. below type-typical: base closes 40% of the gap from 3.3% to 25.0% (not below the best of 3 years 9.2%). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 4.8% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 3.3% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30) to 15.0% over 4 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 4.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 15.6% and margins above 12.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Evidenced moat source: cost and scale in battery-electric vehicles and storage against named competitors (automotive gross margin ex credits 18.1% versus Ford Model e and Rivian losses; underlying energy margin about 24% versus Fluence 5.1%) plus the Supercharger network (84,465 connectors). Not evidenced against BYD (its margins were not retrieved). The advantage does not show in returns: operating margin fell from 16.8% (FY2022) to 4.6% (FY2025) and 2.6% in Q3 2026; the numbers lane's hand ROIC is about 7.3% for FY2025 and about 5.1% trailing (assumed 21% tax), below the 9.2% market cost of equity (risk-free 5.0% plus ERP 4.2%) before any company premium, and incremental ROIC is negative over the last nine months as capex doubled ahead of returns. Returns are already at or below the cost of capital; no mechanism in the company's numbers yet lifts them (autonomy and storage pricing would have to).): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 25.0% is competed away (0.0% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 10.6% against a demonstrated ROIC 7.0% (Ku 8.6% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (cyclical business (subscription_software): the cycle's average return, no persistence premium)). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 4.2% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-09-30), fading by 10% of its level over 4 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 5.3% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 5.3% = min(3-year average capex 9.9%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 0.6168366640513223, type range (1.5, 5.0), base 1.50, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.38). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.229 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 7.9% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.16 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 15.0%: 3-year effective -7.2% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(2 months of cash costs, today's cash), 16,163,517,691 in the first period rising to 17,853,000,000 (base) of today's cash 17,853,000,000: about 4.52 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 0.0% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 9,267,000,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 3.65% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 7.00% (risk-free + 2%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 27,594,000,000 earn the risk-free rate 5.00% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 8.56%: table rate 8.56% (risk-free 5.00% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:mature +0.00%, weak_governance +0.25%, weak_competition +0.25%, country_risk +0.15%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.29%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 8.05% with the expected return on debt 6.00% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 3.65% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 8.56% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 8.56% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.56% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.56% (no stage or funding add-on to drop: the same table as the explicit years), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 8.56%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 5.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 47.1% of NOPAT with ROIC 9.6% (adequate moat, Ku+1pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.6%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.6%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: base terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 9.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 47.3% of NOPAT with ROIC 10.6% (adequate moat, Ku + 50% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+2pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.6%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.6%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 15.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 39.8% of NOPAT with ROIC 12.6% (adequate moat, Ku + 71% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+4pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.6%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.6%.

assumptions.falsifier: A dated consensus becomes available and differs from the base first-year revenue by more than 10%.
assumptions.label: consensus comparison

assumptions.label: analyst override: maintenance_capex_pct
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of maintenance_capex_pct: Capex floor at management's guide (review repair). Guide: FY2026 capex 'approximately $20 billion' (call) / 'in excess of $20 billion' (10-Q); nine-month capex 13,014M, so Q4 2026 needs at least about 6.99B, prorated 65/92 to about 4.94B for the 2026-10-27..12-31 stub. The CFO said capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, compute, a semiconductor fab); Musk: 'tens of billions' in 2028 (not quantified, so held at the 20B floor, not raised). Total capex (maintenance + growth at sales_to_capital) is held at about 4.94B in the stub and 20B in FY2027 and FY2028 in every scenario; the extra over the engine's maintenance rate (5.3% of revenue) sits on this line because it buys Robotaxi, Optimus, compute and the fab, which have no separate modelled revenue, so no revenue is credited for it. From FY2029 the engine rate returns (no company evidence for later years). Depreciation is not raised for the extra spend (no tax shield taken: conservative). (evidence dc_g_capex_fy2026_oct_call, dc_g_capex_fy2026_oct_10q, dc_capex_9m_2026, web:dc_call_20261021, web:pf_10q_20261022; source tier guidance); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: analyst override: mature_margin
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of mature_margin: GAAP operating margin after SBC. Own record FY2020-FY2025: 6.3%, 12.1%, 16.8%, 9.2%, 7.2%, 4.6% (median about 8.2%); Q3 2026 2.6% with R&D at 10% of revenue. anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-06-30: cash 3,134,218,213,000, investments 383,568,535,000 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 1,029,590,553,000 (tagged_total; operating leases treated in cash costs), deferred revenue 0 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 25,932,524,521 at 2025-12-31 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-06-30 and as_of 2026-11-01: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected; share count is dated 2025-12-31 (181 days from the balance sheet), so cash and shares are from different dates. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 5,593,660,250,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 5,593,660,250,000 (FY2026 revenue: company guidance midpoint 5,593,660,250,000 (5,561,860,250,000-5,625,460,250,000, issued 2026-10-15); FY2026 = reported Q1-Q3 2026 (NT$3,898.7bn) + the Q4 2026 revenue guide midpoint US$53.3bn at the guided 31.8 NT$/US$ (NT$1,694.9bn) = NT$5,593.7bn (US$175.9bn, consistent with the 'around 44%' US$ growth guide). Track record (7/7 beats, ratio about 1.024) not applied: the Q4 guide is in US$, so it cannot be the remainder item; applying it to Q4 only would add about NT$40bn (+0.7%). (evidence rf_g_rev_fy26, nm_revenue_q1_2026, nm_revenue_q2_2026, nm_revenue_q3_2026, dc_g_rev_q4_26, dc_g_fx_q4_26, dc_g_revgrowth_fy26, web:dc_rel_q3_2026; source tier guidance)); growth 46.9% vs the last report. The stub 2026-11-01..2026-12-31 runs at 6,567,935,169,192/yr = current-year revenue x (1+g)^(0.5 - stub/2) (late-year run rate).

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 4.98% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Margins hold above the through-the-cycle level through a full industry downturn (structural), or fall to the trough (the cycle turned).
assumptions.label: cycle position: cyclical industry at a margin peak
assumptions.rationale: The industry is cyclical and the latest operating margin 50.8% sits at the top of the history (through-the-cycle 44.4%; the model card's position: peak). Analyst treatment 'structural': The 20-F names the semiconductor cycle and FY2023 revenue fell 4.5%, but TSMC's share keeps rising (72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue), growth is driven by value per wafer (shipments +9.6% y/y vs revenue +51%) and node leadership; the cycle is carried as an explicit 2028 down year in the bear instead of normalizing today's revenue to a trend. (evidence web:pf_10k_20260416, pf_revenue_fy2023, web:fd_trendforce_2q26, dc_k_ship_3q26, dc_k_ship_3q25). The bear still tests a return to the through-the-cycle margin.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 27.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 15.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: -4.5% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 2.2% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 11.3% or above 32.5%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from the long-run like-for-like growth 23.3% (5-year CAGR without acquisition steps, else 3-year), not the current fiscal year's 46.9%: a cyclical business's change this year is the cycle, not a trend: 27.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 12.2% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 27.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 15.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 38.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 19.0% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.6% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (51.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 50.8% (operating_income / revenue, fiscal year ending 2025-12-31) to 44.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 47.5% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 50.8% (operating_income / revenue, fiscal year ending 2025-12-31) to 52.0% over 6 years, then holds. strong moat: current margin 50.8% held, recovering half-way to the best of 3 years 50.8% only up to the type ceiling 40.0% (the ceiling caps assumed expansion; it never cuts an evidenced margin). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 51.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 50.8% (operating_income / revenue, fiscal year ending 2025-12-31) to 57.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 40.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 40.0% and margins above 55.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat strong (analyst assessment (strong): Process-technology and scale moat: 72.5% foundry share vs Samsung 5.9% and Intel external foundry US$293M/quarter; 79% of wafer revenue at 7nm and below; ROIC ~53% with incremental ROIC ~61%, far above an ~8% cost of capital, sustained since 2019 (no fade toward the cost of capital in the data).): current margin held and terminal ROIC max(demonstrated ROIC, Ku+5pp) capped at 40%.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 0.0% of revenue today (SBC / revenue, fiscal year ending 2025-12-31), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 18.1% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 18.1% = min(3-year average capex 36.8%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 1.3444176488363486, type range (0.8, 2.0), base 0.81, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 0.81). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 0.0% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 0%).

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.057 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 0.0% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.00 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 17.0%: 3-year effective 16.3% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(4 months of cash costs, today's cash), 680,303,602,021 in the first period rising to 2,588,238,248,659 (base) of today's cash 3,134,218,213,000: about 99.81 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 100% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 51.8% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 1,029,590,553,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 1.00% (interest expense / reported debt, fiscal_year); any assumed new money at 9.98% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 383,568,535,000 earn the risk-free rate 4.98% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 10.71%: table rate 10.71% (risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, cyclical +0.50%, capital_intensity_high +0.50%, weak_customer_concentration +0.25%, country_risk +0.18%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.39%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.77% with the expected return on debt 5.98% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 1.00% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 0.0%) = 10.71% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 0 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 0 gives debt weight 0.0% (no_net_debt, 1 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal rate 9.21% (one rate for all scenarios, floored at terminal growth + 3 points); each scenario's horizon debt earns its tax shield 0.17% (Kd_promised x tax, at most 3%) as a bridge item D x shield / (rate - g), at most the debt: debt is credited with its tax shield only, never as cheaper capital, so more debt never raises the value; the terminal Ke (not relevered) is the mature table 9.21% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended); the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 10.71%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.
