anchors.formula: last fiscal year in the casefile analysis; shares/net debt from the valuation opening balance; market cap = price x shares

assumptions.falsifier: A primary balance sheet at or after the statement date shows cash, investments or debt differing by more than 2% of market value.
assumptions.label: opening balance
assumptions.rationale: dataqa-resolved balance at 2026-06-30: cash 2,810,600,000, investments 0 (of which listed equity stakes at fair value 0; private stakes at book value only) (kept as assets earning risk-free after tax; liquidated before any external financing is assumed), debt 4,624,400,000 (noncurrent+current; operating leases treated in cash costs; includes 1,684,600,000 of debt-like claims from inputs), deferred revenue 3,756,300,000 in its own ledger.

assumptions.falsifier: The latest filing cover count differs by more than 1%.
assumptions.label: point-in-time shares
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 384,988,173 at 2026-07-27 (basis cover); weighted-average EPS shares are not used for ownership.

assumptions.falsifier: Filings disclose in-the-money convertibles, warrants or vested options above 1% of shares that are not modelled here.
assumptions.label: dilution
assumptions.rationale: No incremental shares added today: future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_pct), so adding unvested awards would double count; shares are added only where a cash shortfall is closed by settling SBC in shares or by an equity raise (see the funding rows). Convertibles/warrants status in dataqa: missing.

assumptions.falsifier: A filing shows preferred stock, material minority interests or contingent consideration.
assumptions.label: other claims
assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock, minority interests or other senior claims are recorded in the FactBook; deferred revenue renews in a going concern (ledger, not a runoff claim).

assumptions.falsifier: The next filing shows net cash or shares changed by more than 2% of market value since the statement date.
assumptions.label: statement-to-as_of bridge
assumptions.rationale: No bridge events applied between the balance-sheet date 2026-06-30 and as_of 2026-10-28: cash generated, buybacks and financing in between are NOT reflected. A reviewer must bridge or accept this.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue differs from 14,000,000,000 by more than 3%.
assumptions.label: current fiscal year revenue
assumptions.rationale: FY ending 2026-12-31 revenue 14,000,000,000 (FY2026 revenue: company guidance midpoint 14,000,000,000 (13,800,000,000-14,200,000,000, issued 2026-07-29); FY2026 revenue = the latest company guidance midpoint, 14.0bn (13.8-14.2bn, issued 2026-07-29, raised from 13.5bn in February and 13.75bn in April). Not adjusted by the 1.040 track-record ratio: the beats have narrowed (Q4 2025 1.011, FY2025 1.003, Q1 2026 1.019) and Q2 2026 missed the guided midpoint (0.977) on supply-chain congestion and project phasing, so a ratio near 1.00 is the honest reading for the unreported second half. The Q3 2026 results of 2026-10-28 are not citable until 2026-10-30. (evidence rp_g_rev_fy26_jul, web:pf_rel_20260729_1; source tier guidance)); growth 36.9% vs the last report. The stub 2026-10-28..2026-12-31 runs at 16,031,695,924/yr = (current-year revenue - reported year to date) / years from 2026-06-30 to 2026-12-31.

assumptions.falsifier: Revenue growth stays more than 5 points above the base path for two consecutive years, or falls below the bear path.
assumptions.label: growth fade rule
assumptions.rationale: Excess growth over terminal growth halves every 2.5 years in base (growth stage; base rate: >20% growers slow to ~8% in five years and ~5% in ten, Koller et al.); bear fades 25% faster, bull 30% slower. Terminal growth = the risk-free rate 5.00% in base and bull, 0.5% lower in the bear (base 5.0%, bear 4.5%, bull 5.0%): the convention of the implied equity risk premium it is paired with (solved with perpetual growth at the Treasury yield; Damodaran sets stable growth at, never above, the risk-free rate), with terminal reinvestment g / ROIC (growth is not free).

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 above 26.0% (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Realistic disappointment: first-year growth min(base - spread, half of base) with spread 6.0% (max of stage floor, historical growth volatility and consensus dispersion), faster fade: 6.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 4.9% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 4.5% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 4.5%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 16.0% or above 30.0%.
assumptions.label: base revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Faded from organic growth 16.7%, not the current fiscal year's 36.9% that includes acquired revenue (year-to-date growth 26.7% with an acquisition in the last fiscal year; no pro forma revenue saved: organic growth taken as the pre-deal median 16.7%); the acquired revenue is a level shift in the current year: 26.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 11.9% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 5.4% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 26.0% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull revenue growth
assumptions.rationale: Plausible upside: base + spread 6.0% (never above base + 2 spreads), slower fade: 34.0% in FY ending 2027-12-31, 17.4% in FY ending 2031-12-31, 6.5% in FY ending 2041-12-31; terminal 5.0%.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported growth over the horizon outside the bear-bull range.
assumptions.label: growth against base rates for companies of this size
assumptions.rationale: Base case: revenue 15.8% a year over 10 fiscal years (13.2% after 2.35% expected inflation); 6% of companies with sales of $7,000-12,000m (2015 dollars) grew at least that fast in 1950-2015, class median 3.2% (Mauboussin, Callahan & Majd, The Base Rate Book, Credit Suisse 2016, exhibit 4 (sales CAGR by size, 1950-2015, inflation-adjusted to 2015 dollars); sales include acquisitions and survivors only). A reality check on the forecast, not a probability for this company: evidence can justify a place in the tail.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin stays at or above the base path (19.1% in FY ending 2027-12-31) for two years (bear too harsh).
assumptions.label: bear operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 18.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 14.0% over 4 years, then holds. bear = base mature margin - 7.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below 15.6% without a one-off explanation.
assumptions.label: base operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 18.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 20.0% over 6 years, then holds. below type-typical: base closes 70% of the gap from 18.9% to 30.0% (not below the best of 3 years 17.9%). cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Reported operating margin for FY ending 2027-12-31 below the base path 19.1% (bull not on track).
assumptions.label: bull operating margin (after SBC)
assumptions.rationale: GAAP operating margin after SBC moves from 18.9% (TTM operating_income / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30) to 23.0% over 6 years, then holds. bull = base mature margin + 0.75 x 7.0%, capped at the type ceiling 45.0%. cash_cost_ratio = 1 - (operating margin + sbc_pct + depreciation_pct), matching drivers.operating: ebit = revenue - cash costs - SBC - depreciation.

assumptions.falsifier: Returns on capital stay above 28.0% and margins above 23.0% for three years (haircut too harsh), or fall below the bear path (too generous).
assumptions.label: competitive advantage behind margins and returns
assumptions.rationale: Moat adequate (analyst assessment (adequate): Scale in power plus thermal and an installed base that feeds services (20% of sales, growing faster than products); margins sit inside the named competitors' range (Eaton Electrical Americas 27.5%, Legrand 20.8%), so the advantage is real but not exclusive.): 25% of today's margin excess over the type-typical 30.0% is competed away (0.0% of revenue) and terminal ROIC fades to 23.0% against a demonstrated ROIC 30.2% (Ku 8.5% + 50% of the demonstrated excess, at least Ku+2pp: the base-rate share of excess returns left after ten years, lifted for a high, stable realized ROIC (demonstrated ROIC 15.7% vs hurdle 8.5% (excess 0.15); ROIC variation 63% over 5 years (stability 0.00); gross margin 36.3%, range 8.2% over 5 years (margin 0.00))). A quantified model haircut, not evidence: an evidenced analyst moat assessment replaces it.

assumptions.falsifier: SBC rises above today's share of revenue for two consecutive years.
assumptions.label: stock-based compensation
assumptions.rationale: SBC 0.5% of revenue today (TTM SBC / TTM revenue to 2026-06-30), fading by 30% of its level over 6 years at scale; charged as a cash-equivalent cost (policy cash_equivalent) with point-in-time shares, so no separate dilution is added unless a cash shortfall is closed by settling it in shares. Value-neutral to the mix: the GAAP margin path already includes SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Capex or D&A as a share of revenue moves by more than 1.5 points.
assumptions.label: depreciation and maintenance capex
assumptions.rationale: Depreciation 3.0% of revenue today (latest D&A incl. amortization) converges to maintenance capex 2.0% = min(3-year average capex 2.0%, depreciation) by the last explicit year, so the terminal year carries no free depreciation tax shield or unfunded replacement. The GAAP margin path is held, so D&A above maintenance capex (mostly amortization of acquired intangibles) is treated as a recurring economic cost by the end, not released as cash.

assumptions.falsifier: Net reinvestment per unit of new revenue over the next two years differs from the base by more than 50%.
assumptions.label: growth reinvestment
assumptions.rationale: Growth costs capital: net reinvestment = change in revenue x capital per unit of new revenue, starting at 1 / sales-to-capital (history 6.021493963115298, type range (0.3, 1.0), base 3.50, bear x0.8, bull x1.2) and converging by the last explicit year to the terminal rule g / ROIC (sales-to-capital = ROIC / NOPAT margin, base 1.53). Per period growth capex + change in working capital - change in deferred revenue equals that need on the bases drivers uses (stub: the current year's need pro rata, no working-capital step; first year: change from the current fiscal year); growth capex is floored at zero where customer prepayments fund more than the need; a declining business releases capital through maintenance capex below depreciation (never below 50% of the maintenance level). Acquisition spend 3y: 4.9% of revenue (the share of the D&A roll-off it replaces stays a cash cost: 100%). The stub's revenue change excludes 2,058,061,426 of bought revenue (the current year's step above organic growth 16.7% on last year's revenue (pre deal growth: an estimate)): the acquisition paid for it and its price is in the opening balance, so it is not charged again as growth reinvestment.

assumptions.falsifier: Receivables+inventory-payables or deferred revenue move by more than 5% of revenue against revenue.
assumptions.label: working capital and deferred revenue
assumptions.rationale: working_capital_ratio 0.238 = change in (receivables + inventory - payables) / change in revenue, 2022-12-31..2025-12-31; deferred revenue kept at 23.4% of the annual revenue rate (opening balance / stub rate); prepaid_share 0.47 = 2 x ratio (ledger split only, value-neutral).

assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% or fall below 12% of pretax income for two years.
assumptions.label: tax rate
assumptions.rationale: Normalized tax 24.7%: 3-year effective 24.7% bounded to 15-25% (21% statutory when pretax income is not positive); NOL usage capped at 80% of taxable income; opening NOL 0 unless supplied.

assumptions.falsifier: The company accumulates cash for two years without distributing, or distributes while cash falls below the minimum.
assumptions.label: minimum cash and payout
assumptions.rationale: Minimum operating cash = min(2 months of cash costs, today's cash), 2,073,044,286 in the first period rising to 2,810,600,000 (base) of today's cash 2,810,600,000: about 7.30 per share is HELD as operating cash and never released, so it adds no value (a judgement: the company already operates with this balance). Cash above it and the investments are valued at face. Excess cash is distributed at 50% (buybacks/dividends; history: distributions = 18.8% of FCF over 3 years) only once free cash flow stays positive; cash retained above the minimum is still worth face (valuation._roll_back), so the payout policy changes funding, not value. A shortfall is closed by investments, then SBC settled in shares, then assumed debt within capacity, then an assumed equity raise.

assumptions.falsifier: Refinancing at a rate more than 2 points above the assumption or a covenant breach.
assumptions.label: existing debt
assumptions.rationale: Existing debt 4,624,400,000 held flat (maturities refinanced) at 1.86% (interest expense / debt); any assumed new money at 10.00% (risk-free + 5%), only up to 3x EBITDA before SBC.

assumptions.falsifier: Investments are liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.
assumptions.label: investment income
assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments 0 earn the risk-free rate 5.00% after tax; principal counted once in the terminal bridge, or spent first when cash falls short (income falls with the balance).

assumptions.falsifier: Long-term risk-free rate moves by more than 1 point, the company changes its leverage materially, or the base plan starts or stops needing external funding.
assumptions.label: cost of equity and terminal WACC
assumptions.rationale: Ke 10.05%: table rate 10.05% (risk-free 5.00% + ERP 4.20% + business-risk add-ons stage:growth +1.50%, weak_competition +0.25%, country_risk +0.48%, country_risk_market_neutral -0.38%, market_neutral -1.00%) is the cost of equity at market-average leverage (D/E 0.25); unlevered Ku 9.24% with the expected return on debt 6.00% (risk-free + 1%; the coupon 1.86% sets interest and the tax shield, never the discount rate); Ke = max(table, Ku + (Ku - Kd_e) x D/E 4.7%) = 10.05% (below-market leverage keeps the table rate: conservative, no credit for a lower rate). Net debt 3,886,844,286 (debt - investments - cash above the minimum) against the model's own base equity value 82,139,018,118 gives debt weight 4.5% (converged, 5 iterations): a fixed point on the model's value, never the quote, so the discount rate does not move with the price. Terminal WACC 8.41% = E/V x terminal Ke 8.55% + D/V x (Kd_e - Kd_promised x tax), floored at terminal growth + 3 points; the terminal Ke is the mature table 8.55% (the table without stage:growth +1.50%: the forecast is mature by its terminal date, so the perpetuity does not carry the risk of a phase the model has ended), relevered at the same D/E; the explicit years and the roll-back of the terminal value keep Ke 10.05%. External-funding add-on not applied from the executed base funding result (explicit years). Same Ke, and the same terminal rate, in all scenarios.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bear terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 4.5%, operating margin 14.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 28.1% of NOPAT with ROIC 16.0% (adequate moat, Ku+1pp; Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: base terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 20.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 21.7% of NOPAT with ROIC 23.0% (adequate moat, Ku + 50% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+2pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: Mature-stage margin or returns on capital of the company (or its closest peers) stay below these levels.
assumptions.label: bull terminal value
assumptions.rationale: After 2041-12-31: growth 5.0%, operating margin 23.0% = the last explicit year (no jump), reinvestment = g / ROIC = 16.7% of NOPAT with ROIC 30.0% (adequate moat, Ku + 71% of the demonstrated excess return (at least Ku+4pp); Ku = the terminal's mature-table cost of capital 8.5%); the last explicit year already reinvests on that rule (reinvestment), discounted at WACC 8.4%.

assumptions.falsifier: A dated consensus becomes available and differs from the base first-year revenue by more than 10%.
assumptions.label: consensus comparison
assumptions.rationale: The FactBook carries no revenue consensus at as_of (not retrieved or not stored); nothing is fabricated. Growth is anchored on trailing growth instead.

assumptions.falsifier: The cited evidence is contradicted by a later filing or the override reason no longer holds.
assumptions.label: analyst override: growth_anchor
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of growth_anchor: Growth of FY2027 over the FY2026 guided 14.0bn. Base 26% (contracted): the order backlog was 15.0bn at 2025-12-31 (+109% y/y from 7.2bn, 'majority firm', shipping within 12-18 months) after Q4 2025 organic orders +252% and book-to-bill about 2.9x (trailing-twelve-month orders +81%); the FY2026 guide (14.0bn) less H1 (5.92bn) less the Q3 guide midpoint (3.75bn, organic +34-36%) implies Q4 2026 about 4.33bn (derived), i.e. an exit run rate of about 17.3bn, +24% over FY2026 before any sequential growth in 2027 (Q1 is seasonally lower: Q1 2026 2.65bn vs Q4 2025 2.88bn) and before a full year of the UIG acquisition (closed after the last balance sheet; its revenue is undisclosed, a gap). Bull 34% (contracted): orders keep the FY2025 pace so the backlog conversion of 12-18 months adds sequential growth through 2027 (about 18.8bn). Bear 6% (own history): the second half of the backlog ships but new orders stall after a hyperscaler/neocloud capex pause; Q2 2026 already came in 2.3% below the guided midpoint, large customers impose penalties and stricter terms (10-K), and 2026 orders and backlog are no longer disclosed, so a slowdown would not be visible in advance. Not consensus: the broad FY2027 revenue consensus is dated 2026-10-27 and not citable at as_of (cross-check in gaps only). (evidence rp_k_backlog_fy25, rp_backlog_fy24, rp_k_btb_q4_25, rp_k_orders_ttm_q4_25, rp_k_orders_q4_25, rp_g_rev_fy26_jul, rp_g_rev_q3_26, rp_g_orggr_q3_26, rp_rev_h1_26, rp_rev_q1_26, pf_revenue_q_2025_12_31, web:pf_rel_20260211_1, web:pf_rel_20260729_1, rp_rev_q2_26, web:pf_10k_20260213; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.falsifier: The cited evidence is contradicted by a later filing or the override reason no longer holds.
assumptions.label: analyst override: sbc_pct
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of sbc_pct: Stock-based compensation as a share of revenue: FY2025 45.9m / 10.23bn = 0.45%, H1 2026 30.8m / 5.92bn = 0.52%; 0.5% in every scenario (the same plan in each; dilution of about +1% a year in diluted shares is carried in the share count). (evidence pf_sbc_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2025, rp_sbc_h1_26, rp_rev_h1_26; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.falsifier: The cited evidence is contradicted by a later filing or the override reason no longer holds.
assumptions.label: analyst override: terminal_roic
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of terminal_roic: Perpetual return on new capital after 2041, from VRT's own post-turnaround record (NOPAT = operating income x (1 - 24.7% normalized tax); invested capital = equity + long-term debt - cash, year end): FY2023 15.8% (872m x 0.753 / 4.15bn), FY2024 25.0% (1,367m x 0.753 / 4.11bn), FY2025 27.0% on year-end capital (1,830m x 0.753 / 5.11bn; 29.9% on average capital, the 30% the yearly path uses). Base 23% = the FY2023-25 average (22.6%): a fade from today's ~30% to the three-year through-cycle level, which was earned at an average GAAP margin of 15.9%, below the base terminal margin of 20%, so it is conservative for the base margin. Bear 16% = FY2023, the first post-turnaround year (margin 12.7%, near the bear 14%). Bull 30% = FY2025 on average capital (held). Why it differs from company_path: the path ROIC (bear 15% / base 30% / bull 43%) is the incremental return over the next five years at today's economics; the terminal ROIC is the level after Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta add data-center capacity (mature_margin reason), so base fades 30% -> 23%. Replaces the engine moat rule (Ku + 50% of excess = 12.1%), which had no company data. No named-competitor ROIC was retrieved (gap), so no competitor level is used. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2023, pf_operating_income_fy2024, pf_operating_income_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2023, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_equity_fy2022, pf_long_term_debt_fy2022, pf_cash_fy2022, pf_equity_fy2023, pf_long_term_debt_fy2023, pf_cash_fy2023, pf_equity_fy2024, pf_long_term_debt_fy2024, pf_cash_fy2024, pf_equity_fy2025, pf_long_term_debt_fy2025, pf_cash_fy2025; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: analyst override: terminal_roic
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of terminal_roic: Perpetual return on new capital after 2041, from VRT's own post-turnaround record (NOPAT = operating income x (1 - 24.7% normalized tax); invested capital = equity + long-term debt - cash, year end): FY2023 15.8% (872m x 0.753 / 4.15bn), FY2024 25.0% (1,367m x 0.753 / 4.11bn), FY2025 27.0% on year-end capital (1,830m x 0.753 / 5.11bn; 29.9% on average capital, the 30% the yearly path uses). Base 23% = the FY2023-25 average (22.6%): a fade from today's ~30% to the three-year through-cycle level, which was earned at an average GAAP margin of 15.9%, below the base terminal margin of 20%, so it is conservative for the base margin. Bear 16% = FY2023, the first post-turnaround year (margin 12.7%, near the bear 14%). Bull 30% = FY2025 on average capital (held). Why it differs from company_path: the path ROIC (bear 15% / base 30% / bull 43%) is the incremental return over the next five years at today's economics; the terminal ROIC is the level after Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta add data-center capacity (mature_margin reason), so base fades 30% -> 23%. Replaces the engine moat rule (Ku + 50% of excess = 12.1%), which had no company data. No named-competitor ROIC was retrieved (gap), so no competitor level is used. assumptions.label: analyst override: growth_anchor
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of growth_anchor: Growth of FY2027 over the FY2026 guided 14.0bn. Base 26% (contracted): the order backlog was 15.0bn at 2025-12-31 (+109% y/y from 7.2bn, 'majority firm', shipping within 12-18 months) after Q4 2025 organic orders +252% and book-to-bill about 2.9x (trailing-twelve-month orders +81%); the FY2026 guide (14.0bn) less H1 (5.92bn) less the Q3 guide midpoint (3.75bn, organic +34-36%) implies Q4 2026 about 4.33bn (derived), i.e. an exit run rate of about 17.3bn, +24% over FY2026 before any sequential growth in 2027 (Q1 is seasonally lower: Q1 2026 2.65bn vs Q4 2025 2.88bn) and before a full year of the UIG acquisition (closed after the last balance sheet; its revenue is undisclosed, a gap). Bull 34% (contracted): orders keep the FY2025 pace so the backlog conversion of 12-18 months adds sequential growth through 2027 (about 18.8bn). Bear 6% (own history): the second half of the backlog ships but new orders stall after a hyperscaler/neocloud capex pause; Q2 2026 already came in 2.3% below the guided midpoint, large customers impose penalties and stricter terms (10-K), and 2026 orders and backlog are no longer disclosed, so a slowdown would not be visible in advance. Not consensus: the broad FY2027 revenue consensus is dated 2026-10-27 and not citable at as_of (cross-check in gaps only). (evidence rp_k_backlog_fy25, rp_backlog_fy24, rp_k_btb_q4_25, rp_k_orders_ttm_q4_25, rp_k_orders_q4_25, rp_g_rev_fy26_jul, rp_g_rev_q3_26, rp_g_orggr_q3_26, rp_rev_h1_26, rp_rev_q1_26, pf_revenue_q_2025_12_31, web:pf_rel_20260211_1, web:pf_rel_20260729_1, rp_rev_q2_26, web:pf_10k_20260213; source tier contracted); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: analyst override: mature_margin
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of mature_margin: GAAP operating margin after SBC and acquired-intangible amortization. History: FY2023 12.7%, FY2024 17.1%, FY2025 17.9%, H1 2026 18.2% (Q1 16.6%, Q2 19.5%); the FY2026 guide (adjusted 23.3-24.3%, GAAP EPS 5.82-5.92 vs adjusted 6.65-6.75) implies a GAAP margin of roughly 21% for FY2026 with a heavier second half (Q3 adjusted guide 24-25%). Base 20%: above FY2025 because the gains were broad (every segment's margin rose in Q2 2026, including shrinking EMEA) and price-cost held, but below the FY2026 peak (quarter review flag peak_margin_run_rate) because Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta are all adding data-center capacity. Bear 14%: between FY2023 (12.7%) and FY2024 (17.1%), the level before the AI-driven price-cost gains, as capacity catches up and price competition returns. Bull 23% (guidance): the guided Q3/FY2026 adjusted margin of 23-25% is held through the cycle and acquired-intangible amortization fades, so GAAP approaches adjusted. (evidence pf_operating_income_fy2023, pf_revenue_fy2023, pf_operating_income_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_operating_income_fy2025, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_operating_income_q_2026_03_31, pf_revenue_q_2026_03_31, pf_operating_income_q_2026_06_30, pf_revenue_q_2026_06_30, rp_g_adjopm_q3_26, rp_g_adjopm_fy26_jul, rp_g_eps_fy26_jul, rp_g_adjeps_fy26_jul, web:pf_rel_20260729_1; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

assumptions.label: analyst override: sales_to_capital
assumptions.rationale: Analyst override of sales_to_capital: Revenue added per dollar of net invested capital (equity + long-term debt - cash), net of customer advances (the engine funds growth capex + working capital - change in deferred revenue from this ratio). Base 3.5 = VRT's FY2023-25 record: revenue +3.37bn on invested capital +0.95bn (4.15bn -> 5.11bn), which already includes the PurgeRite purchase (Nov 2025). The earlier 2.2 counted acquisitions already paid for in the opening balance and, for UIG, deducted again as a 1.45bn debt-like claim (double count). Cross-check with the company's own capex: FY2023-25 capex 1.9-2.2% of revenue (128m, 167m, 220m) and the FY2026 guide 550-570m (~4% of 14.0bn); with working capital funded largely by advances (current deferred revenue 3.63bn at H1 2026), a capex-guide build implies an even higher ratio, so 3.5 is the conservative company figure. Bear 2.2 = FY2024 -> FY2025 (revenue +2.22bn on capital +0.99bn incl. PurgeRite): growth bought, advances unwind. Bull 4.0 (guidance-anchored): between the record and the FY2026 capex-guide build. Future acquisitions (UIG earnout up to 1.15bn) stay a gap, not a number. (evidence pf_revenue_fy2023, pf_revenue_fy2024, pf_revenue_fy2025, pf_equity_fy2023, pf_long_term_debt_fy2023, pf_cash_fy2023, pf_equity_fy2024, pf_long_term_debt_fy2024, pf_cash_fy2024, pf_equity_fy2025, pf_long_term_debt_fy2025, pf_cash_fy2025, pf_capex_fy2023, pf_capex_fy2024, pf_capex_fy2025, rp_g_capex_fy26_jul, nm_deferred_revenue_change_h1_2026, rp_uig_upfront; source tier own_history); original engine value recorded.

Management changed its own outlook: the forecast anchors may no longer hold.
New debt, convertible or equity changes claims, dilution and the funding assumption of the thesis.
